newsitem.title: USA: Apparel trade takes steps against sweatshops - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Apparel trade takes steps against sweatshops - NYT.

text.p: Nike Inc, Reebok International and L.L. Bean are part of a presidential taskforce which has agreed to a code of conduct for apparel factories that U.S. firms use around the world, the New York Times said.

Wednesday's edition of the newspaper said the taskforce, which includes human rights groups and labour unions, formed a code of conduct on wages and working conditions, including a maximum 60-hour working week.
It also agreed to set up an association with monitors to inspect the apparel factories worldwide, approving companies which complied with the code of conduct, the paper said.
Companies which followed the code can tag or label their product so consumers will know it was not made in a sweatshop, the newspaper said.
Other corporate members include Nicole Miller, Patagonia and Phillips-Van Heusen Corp, the paper said.
